requirements.source_quote:
Reconstruct the restaurant's timber beams and columns, exposed duct, brick wall, tables and upholstered seating, wood floor and black-and-white tiled aisle. Preserve the deep aisle perspective and furniture/column occlusions. Keep the duct round, beams volumetric and passageways open; distant signage and fine upholstery patterns may be simplified.

Inputs: input/reference.png. Use metres and Z up. Keep major components independently editable, with thickness, support and meaningful spacing. Do not substitute the complete reference on a plane or a single-camera projection for three-dimensional geometry. Local material textures are allowed.

No original 3D model, depth map or calibrated camera is supplied. Use a dining-table height of 0.75 m as the task scale convention, not a measured real-world dimension. Infer other dimensions proportionally and complete hidden surfaces plausibly.

Create a perspective camera matching the input and render main.png. Copy it and translate 0.30 m to its right along local X without changing rotation or lens; render alternate.png and retain both cameras. This second view checks real three-dimensional structure; unseen real-world details need not be uniquely recovered.

Render every required image from the same scene using Cycles at 1280 × 853 pixels, AgX and exposure 0. Use only the supplied inputs to establish this scene; do not retrieve its original source model or additional source views.
